classification.difficultyReason: Find the intersection of two lines by elimination, then substitute its coordinates into a third equation to determine a parameter.

content.prompt: Find the value of $c$ for which the lines $x+y=8$, $x-y=12$ and $3x+2y=c$ are concurrent.

answer.short:
$c=26$.

The first two lines intersect at $(10,-2)$; substitute this point into the third equation.
answer.worked:
Adding the first two equations eliminates $y$:
$$\begin{align*}(x+y)+(x-y)&=8+12\\2x&=20\\x&=10\end{align*}$$
Substituting into $x+y=8$:
$$\begin{align*}10+y&=8\\y&=-2\end{align*}$$
Concurrent lines pass through the same point, so $(10,-2)$ must also satisfy $3x+2y=c$:
$$\begin{align*}c&=3(10)+2(-2)\\c&=26\end{align*}$$
